topics.label: Course introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening section welcomes students to the final lecture and introduces the learning objectives regarding cancer therapies.

topics.label: Conventional modalities and cytotoxic chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss traditional cancer treatment approaches—including surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic drugs—along with systemic toxicities and efflux-mediated drug resistance.

topics.label: Exploiting cancer-specific vulnerabilities and defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore therapeutic strategies that capitalize on specific tumor vulnerabilities, such as hormone receptor reliance, cell cycle checkpoint defects, and synthetic lethality in DNA repair.

topics.label: Kinase inhibitors, oncogene addiction, and drug resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover the concept of oncogene addiction, the design of small-molecule kinase inhibitors, and the structural and signaling mechanisms driving resistance to these targeted therapies.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibody therapies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics focus on engineered monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates designed to target tumor surface markers and deliver cytotoxic agents.

topics.label: Tumor immunology and modern immunotherapy approaches
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address the biological basis of tumor immune surveillance and the development of immunotherapies, including checkpoint inhibitors, bispecific antibodies, and CAR T cells.

topics.label: Systemic challenges, mortality trends, and future treatment paradigms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the broader progress in cancer mortality, persistent obstacles in drug development and combination therapy, and future clinical dilemmas.
